defects.title: Installer and app exe are not Authenticode-signed, and the first install has no integrity check
defects.claim: The `bundle.windows` block in src-tauri/tauri.conf.json:63-70 has only an "nsis" section: there is no `certificateThumbprint`, `signCommand` or `timestampUrl`, so the NSIS `-setup.exe` and the app exe carry no Authenticode signature. The release pipeline produces no checksums and no provenance, and the site publishes no checksums (site/index.html:35,46 just link to `clippiboy.com/get/site`). scripts/make-probe.mjs:71 tells testers: "If Windows warns that the publisher is unknown: 'More info' and then 'Run anyway'." Minisign only protects updates; a fresh install trusts whatever asset currently sits on the latest release.
defects.scenario: Anyone or anything holding `contents: write` (the compromised-action path in SC-3, a leaked PAT, a careless maintainer) can replace `-setup.exe` on the latest release. Every new download through clippiboy.com/get would then serve the replacement, and nothing verifies it. Users also see SmartScreen warnings, and on Windows 11 with Smart App Control on, unsigned low-reputation binaries are blocked outright.
defects.fix: Sign with Azure Trusted Signing through tauri's `bundle.windows.signCommand` (e.g. `trusted-signing-cli -e <endpoint> -a <account> -c <profile> %1`) or another OV/EV certificate; enable GitHub "immutable releases"; publish `SHA256SUMS` and `actions/attest-build-provenance` attestations and show the hash on the site; stop telling users to click through SmartScreen.

defects.title: A workflow_dispatch "trial run" publishes a real signed release tagged `main`
defects.claim: .github/workflows/release.yml:15-16 enables `workflow_dispatch:` under the comment `# For a trial run without a tag.`, while `:60` sets `tagName: ${{ github.ref_name }}`, `:68` `releaseDraft: false` and `:71` `includeUpdaterJson: true`. In tauri-action v0 (`src/index.ts:178`: `if (tagName && !releaseId) { ... createRelease(...) }`; `create-release.ts` calls `createRelease({ tag_name, target_commitish: commitish || context.sha, draft })`) a non-empty tagName always creates a release. On a dispatch from main, `github.ref_name` is "main", so tauri-action creates git tag `main` and publishes a non-draft release "ClippiBoy main", signed with the production updater key and carrying a `latest.json`. The comment at `:74-75` ("a workflow_dispatch trial run has no release to attach anything to") is wrong. Confirmed against tauri-action v0 source.
defects.scenario: GitHub marks new published releases as latest by default, so the updater endpoint `releases/latest/download/latest.json` then serves the trial build. If the version was already bumped, which is the documented order (README.md:752 "bump the version … first"), every installation is offered an untagged build. A tag named `main` also makes `git checkout main` ambiguous.
defects.fix: Use `tagName: ${{ startsWith(github.ref, 'refs/tags/') && github.ref_name || '' }}` (an empty tagName makes tauri-action build only), and upload trial artifacts with `actions/upload-artifact`.

defects.title: Third-party actions on mutable refs run alongside the updater signing key and a contents: write token
defects.claim: .github/workflows/release.yml uses third-party actions on mutable refs: `:33` `dtolnay/rust-toolchain@stable` (a branch), `:36` `swatinem/rust-cache@v2`, `:54` `tauri-apps/tauri-action@v0` (currently 84b9d35 = v0.6.2, while v1.0.0 exists). `:57-58` pass the signing key `TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY` and its password in env to tauri-action. `actions/checkout@v4` (release.yml:26, ffmpeg.yml:21) keeps the default `persist-credentials: true`, leaving the `contents: write` token in `.git/config`. `npm ci` (release.yml:40, :50-51) runs dependency install scripts in the same job.
defects.scenario: A retagged or compromised action (the tj-actions/changed-files incident pattern) or a malicious npm lifecycle script could read `TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY` and sign a malicious update for every user, or use the token left in `.git/config` to replace release assets (see SC-1).
defects.fix: Pin every action to a full SHA and add Dependabot for `github-actions`; set `persist-credentials: false`; run `npm ci --ignore-scripts` where possible; move signing into its own job or step, or an environment (SC-4).

defects.title: Updater signing secrets are repo-level with no environment protection, review gate or tag ruleset
defects.claim: The updater signing secrets used by .github/workflows/release.yml:7-9 are repo-level secrets with no `environment:` protection. There is no review gate and no tag ruleset (part of the report's "Signing-key governance" finding).
defects.scenario: Anyone who can push a tag can point a `v*` tag at a commit carrying a modified `release.yml` and print the signing key.
defects.fix: Create a `release` environment with required reviewers and a deployment rule limited to `v*` tags, move both secrets there, and add a tag ruleset.

defects.title: Updater key password is stored in plaintext beside the key; single key with no rotation or backup
defects.claim: README.md:759-765 documents that "the key lives under `%USERPROFILE%\.clippiboy\updater.key` with its password beside it in `updater.password`". A plaintext password sitting next to the encrypted key defeats the encryption. There is a single key with no rotation or backup plan, and README.md:750 notes it cannot be recovered if lost (part of the report's "Signing-key governance" finding).
defects.scenario: Whoever obtains the maintainer's `.clippiboy` folder gets both the encrypted key and its password and can sign updates; if the single key is lost it cannot be recovered.
defects.fix: Store the password in a password manager, not beside the key, and keep an offline backup of the key.

defects.title: GPLv3 ffmpeg is redistributed without license text or a source offer
defects.claim: .github/workflows/ffmpeg.yml:38-39 zips only the two exes (`Compress-Archive -Path dist-ffmpeg/ffmpeg.exe, dist-ffmpeg/ffprobe.exe`), dropping gyan.dev's LICENSE and README; the release notes at `:52` say only "(gyan.dev essentials build $version)". gyan.dev essentials builds are configured `--enable-gpl --enable-version3` (libx264/libx265). `scripts/make-probe.mjs --full` (:113-117) ships the same exes with no license either. Distributing GPLv3 object code requires the license and Corresponding Source, or a written offer, or equivalent access with clear directions (GPLv3 §6). Running ffmpeg as a separate process keeps the proprietary app itself out of scope, but the redistribution obligations still apply.
defects.scenario: Every `ffmpeg-*` release ZIP and every `make-probe.mjs --full` bundle redistributes GPLv3 binaries without the license text or source access/offer required by GPLv3 §6.
defects.fix: Include `LICENSE.txt` and gyan's README in the ZIP and the release; link to or mirror the exact source and build scripts for that version; mention it in-app and on the site. Alternatively switch to an LGPL build if the GPL encoders are not needed.

defects.title: No third-party license notices anywhere
defects.claim: A search of `src/`, `src-tauri/src`, `src-tauri/windows` and `site/` found no third-party license or notice file or screen. The only LICENSE is the proprietary one (LICENSE:23-25 says third-party parts "stay under their own licenses"). The installer statically links about 740 crates (MIT, Apache-2.0, BSD, ISC; Apache-2.0 also needs its NOTICE files), plus React, zustand, the bundled SQLite and ring. The Stream Deck plugin ships `@elgato/streamdeck`, `ws` and `zod` in `node_modules`. The site serves Inter (OFL). MIT and BSD require the copyright notice in binary distributions.
defects.scenario: Every distributed installer, Stream Deck plugin and the website omit the copyright and license notices that the bundled third-party components' licenses require.
defects.fix: Generate `THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES` with `cargo about` plus `license-checker` or `npm-license-crawler` in CI, bundle it as a resource, and link it from Settings → About and from the site.

defects.title: No CI quality gate at all
defects.claim: `.github/` contains only `ffmpeg.yml`, `pages.yml` and `release.yml`. There is no PR or push workflow, no `dependabot.yml`, no `rustfmt`/`clippy`/`deny` config and no `rust-toolchain.toml`. `grep '#[test]' src-tauri/src` counts 271 tests that never run in CI; `server/src/*.test.ts` and server's `tsc --noEmit` (server/package.json:9-10) never run either.
defects.scenario: A release is the first time code is compiled in CI, so a broken commit is found at tag time or by users.
defects.fix: Add the `ci.yml` from section 3 of the report (see SC-P-1).

defects.title: server/scripts/e2e.mjs seeds production with accounts whose bearer tokens are public
defects.claim: server/scripts/e2e.mjs:4-6 documents `node scripts/e2e.mjs --seed | npx wrangler d1 execute clippiboy-friends --remote ...`; `:16-21` inserts sessions for `hash("tok-a-test-only")` and `hash("tok-b-test-only")`, tokens that are visible in the public repo; `:11` defaults to the production workers.dev URL. Confirmed by reading; unverified whether any such accounts exist right now.
defects.scenario: Between the seed and the manual `DELETE`, or forever if cleanup is forgotten, anyone reading the public repo can authenticate as these accounts and use share-link upload to R2 (up to 50 MB a clip, publicly linkable), friend requests, presence and so on.
defects.fix: Run e2e against `wrangler dev --local` or a staging D1; or generate random tokens per run and expire them; and put the cleanup in a `finally` block.

defects.title: Release workflow never checks that the tag matches the version
defects.claim: .github/workflows/release.yml:3-5 says "The tag has to match the `version` in `src-tauri/tauri.conf.json`", but no step enforces it, whereas ffmpeg.yml:33-37 has exactly such a check.
defects.scenario: If `v0.9.0` is tagged without bumping `tauri.conf.json` (0.8.3), `latest.json` advertises 0.8.3, nobody is updated, and the release is mislabelled.
defects.fix: Add the "Tag must match versions" guard step from section 3 (SC-P-3), also comparing `package.json` and `Cargo.toml`.

defects.title: rustls 0.23.43 has open RustSec advisories
defects.claim: `rustls 0.23.43` (src-tauri/Cargo.lock:4733) is affected by RUSTSEC-2026-0285, -0346, -0348 and -0349, fixed in >=0.23.46. All are low impact for a client that has no brotli feature. Confirmed with the RustSec advisory DB.
defects.scenario: The shipped TLS stack carries known (low-impact) advisories although a semver-compatible fix is available.
defects.fix: `cargo update -p rustls` (a free fix).

defects.title: zip 4.6.1 has RustSec advisories (app not affected)
defects.claim: `zip 4.6.1` has RUSTSEC-2026-0367, -0368 and -0369, fixed in 9.0. These affect only `extract()`; src-tauri/src/tools.rs:265-283 uses `by_name` with its own hashing, so the app is not affected.
defects.scenario: The dependency carries known advisories; not reachable today because the app only uses `by_name`.
defects.fix: Upgrade zip (to 9.0) anyway.

defects.title: rusqlite 0.32 bundles an old SQLite 3.46.0
defects.claim: `rusqlite 0.32` bundles SQLite 3.46.0 (the latest rusqlite is 0.40). Later SQLite CVEs need attacker-supplied SQL, so impact is low.
defects.scenario: Bundled SQLite lags upstream security fixes; exploitation would require attacker-supplied SQL.
defects.fix: None stated explicitly; the report points to the newer rusqlite 0.40.

defects.title: tiny_http 0.12.0 is low-maintenance (judged acceptable)
defects.claim: `tiny_http 0.12.0` (last release 2022) is low-maintenance, but it is bound to loopback only; the report calls this acceptable.
defects.scenario: An unmaintained HTTP server crate backs the local control port; exposure is limited to loopback.
defects.fix: None proposed (acceptable).

defects.title: tauri, tauri-plugin-updater and iroh lag current releases
defects.claim: Core dependencies are behind current releases: tauri 2.11.5 (latest 2.12.4), tauri-plugin-updater 2.10.1 (latest 2.14.0), iroh 1.2.0 (latest 1.3.0).
defects.scenario: Fixes shipped in newer releases of these crates (including the updater plugin) are not picked up.
defects.fix: None stated explicitly; implied update to the listed latest versions.

defects.title: npm audit reports dev/build-time advisories in root, streamdeck and server lockfiles
defects.claim: `npm audit --package-lock-only` reports advisories that are all dev or build-time only: root `source-map-js` (high, DoS); streamdeck `brace-expansion` and `fast-uri`; server `wrangler 4.141` -> `miniflare` -> `undici 7.29` and `sharp`. The plugin's runtime lockfile is clean.
defects.scenario: Vulnerable packages are present in build/dev tooling only; shipped runtime code is not affected.
defects.fix: None stated explicitly; section 3 adds `npm audit --omit=dev --audit-level=high` to CI.

defects.title: Unmaintained and unsound transitive crates via tauri
defects.claim: Unmaintained transitive crates (`paste`, `proc-macro-error`, `unic-*`) come through tauri; `glib 0.18` (flagged unsound) is Linux-only.
defects.scenario: The dependency tree contains unmaintained/unsound crates pulled in by tauri; glib only affects Linux builds.
defects.fix: None stated explicitly (section 3 proposes cargo-deny advisories checks in CI).

defects.title: Outdated direct dependencies cause duplicate crates (windows, png, dirs)
defects.claim: src-tauri/Cargo.toml:65 `windows = 0.58` is used only by clippiboy, while tauri, wry and tao use 0.61.3 and netwatch uses 0.62.2, giving three `windows` crates. `png = "0.17"` (:47) sits next to 0.18 from image and tray-icon; `dirs = "5"` (:39) sits next to 6 from tauri and 4 from auto-launch. 58 crates are duplicated in total.
defects.scenario: Duplicate crate versions inflate build time and binary size.
defects.fix: Move to `windows`/`windows-core` 0.61, `png` 0.18 and `dirs` 6.

defects.title: Mobile-template crate-type adds link time to a Windows-only app
defects.claim: src-tauri/Cargo.toml:10 sets `crate-type = ["staticlib", "cdylib", "rlib"]`, the mobile template default. With `lto = true` and `codegen-units = 1`, a Windows-only app pays extra link time for the staticlib and cdylib outputs.
defects.scenario: Every release/LTO build links two unneeded library artifacts, lengthening build time.
defects.fix: Set `crate-type = ["rlib"]` (or drop the `[lib]` crate-type).

defects.title: Declared rust-version 1.77 is wrong
defects.claim: src-tauri/Cargo.toml:6 says `rust-version = "1.77"`, but src-tauri/src/telemetry.rs:11 uses `std::sync::LazyLock` (needs 1.80) and iroh 1.2.0 declares an MSRV of 1.91.
defects.scenario: A toolchain that satisfies the declared MSRV (1.77-1.90) fails to build the crate.
defects.fix: Set `rust-version = "1.91"`.

defects.title: Release toolchain is not reproducible (floating toolchain, no --locked)
defects.claim: CI uses floating `dtolnay/rust-toolchain@stable` and `windows-latest`, there is no `rust-toolchain.toml`, and tauri-action does not pass `--locked`, so release builds use whatever toolchain is current and do not enforce Cargo.lock.
defects.scenario: Two releases from the same commit can be built with different compilers, and a lockfile drift is not caught at build time.
defects.fix: Add a `rust-toolchain.toml` with a pinned version and pass `args: -- --locked` to tauri-action (verify that tauri forwards it to cargo).

defects.title: Committed generated schema files drift
defects.claim: `src-tauri/gen/schemas/*` is tracked in git, and a build in this checkout regenerated `linux-schema.json` with +252 lines (the deep-link permissions), so the committed copy is stale. The Tauri template ignores `/gen/schemas`.
defects.scenario: Every build produces a dirty working tree and the committed schemas do not reflect the current permissions.
defects.fix: Either ignore `/gen/schemas`, or regenerate it in CI and fail on a diff.

defects.title: Script-injection pattern with github.ref_name in workflow run steps
defects.claim: .github/workflows/ffmpeg.yml:33,49-50 interpolate `$version = "${{ github.ref_name }}" -replace ...` inside a pwsh double-quoted string, and release.yml:81 runs `gh release upload ${{ github.ref_name }} ...`. Git ref names may contain characters such as `$`, `(`, `)`, `;`, backslash and double quote, so the expression is spliced into the script unescaped. Confirmed pattern; only tag pushers can trigger it.
defects.scenario: Pushing a tag such as `ffmpeg-9$(calc)` executes the embedded command in the workflow runner.
defects.fix: Use `env: TAG: ${{ github.ref_name }}`, then `"$env:TAG"` in the script.

defects.title: bake-release.mjs String.replace replacement strings expand `$` patterns
defects.claim: .github/scripts/bake-release.mjs:97 (`` `$1${escape(release.plugin.url)}"` ``) and :102-106 interpolate the tag/URL into `String.replace` replacement strings. Special replacement patterns `$&`, `` $` `` or `$'` contained in a tag or URL would be expanded and splice page content; `escape()` does not cover this.
defects.scenario: A release tag or asset URL containing `$&`, `` $` `` or `$'` makes the baked `index.html` contain spliced/duplicated page content.
defects.fix: Use function replacers: `html.replace(re, (_, a, b) => a + value + b)`.

defects.title: Public download count includes updater traffic
defects.claim: .github/scripts/bake-release.mjs:61-63 counts GitHub downloads of the `-setup.exe` asset and comments "The `.sig` and `latest.json` beside it are fetched by the updater, not by people, and are left out." But with Tauri v2 and `createUpdaterArtifacts: true`, the NSIS updater downloads the `-setup.exe` itself, so every auto-update of every install counts as a "download". The `/get` proxy (server/site-proxy/index.ts:61) also fetches from GitHub for bots it does not count in D1.
defects.scenario: The download count shown on the site is inflated by auto-updates and by bot fetches through the proxy.
defects.fix: Show the D1 `downloads` sum instead, or subtract updater fetches.

defects.title: Stream Deck plugin never rediscovers the app after a connection failure
defects.claim: streamdeck/src/client.ts:212-216 returns `null` on any fetch error, and `#poll` (:183-185) calls `forget()` only on HTTP 403. `#connect` (:228-230) returns the cached connection (port and token) forever, so the plugin never re-reads the `streamdeck.json` handshake after network failures.
defects.scenario: The user changes the control port in ClippiBoy (src-tauri/src/control.rs:108 `restart`); the keys show "—" until the user clicks "Save and check" in the property inspector or Stream Deck restarts. The cached port is also kept after the app has exited, so a different local process (on a multi-user machine) that later binds that port receives the token twice a second.
defects.fix: Call `forget()` after N consecutive network errors, or when the handshake file's mtime changes, and drop the cache once the handshake disappears.

defects.title: Stream Deck status polls overlap with no in-flight guard
defects.claim: The plugin polls with `setInterval(…, 500)` (streamdeck/src/client.ts:116) while each request has a 2 s timeout (:88) and there is no in-flight guard.
defects.scenario: Against a stalled app, up to 4 status requests can be outstanding at once.
defects.fix: Add an in-flight guard so a new poll does not start while one is pending (implied by the report).

defects.title: Stream Deck keys are redrawn every 500 ms even when nothing changed
defects.claim: `setTitle`/`setState` are sent for every key every 500 ms even when nothing changed (streamdeck/src/keys.ts, streamdeck/src/actions/*.ts).
defects.scenario: Constant redundant messages to Stream Deck for every visible key, twice a second.
defects.fix: Diff against the last drawn values and only send changes.

defects.title: Stream Deck manifest targets end-of-life Node 20 with Debug enabled
defects.claim: streamdeck/com.einfabo.clippiboy.sdPlugin/manifest.json:24-27 declares `"Nodejs": {"Version": "20", "Debug": "enabled"}`. Node 20 has been end-of-life since April 2026. `Debug: enabled` only applies in Stream Deck developer mode (`--inspect=127.0.0.1:{PORT}`) but should be removed from releases.
defects.scenario: The released plugin runs on an EOL Node runtime and ships a debug setting meant for development.
defects.fix: Move to Node "24" (requires raising `Software.MinimumVersion`) and remove `Debug: enabled` from releases.

defects.title: @elgato/streamdeck SDK is a major version behind
defects.claim: `@elgato/streamdeck` is at ^2.1.2 while 3.0.2 is available.
defects.scenario: The plugin misses SDK v3 features and fixes (e.g. Secrets, see SC-31).
defects.fix: Upgrade to @elgato/streamdeck 3.x (implied).

defects.title: Manual control-port token stored in plain Stream Deck global settings
defects.claim: The manually entered ClippiBoy control token is stored in plain Stream Deck global settings, although SDK v3 "Secrets" (Stream Deck 6.9+) exists for this purpose.
defects.scenario: The control-port token sits in plaintext Stream Deck settings storage readable by anything that reads those settings.
defects.fix: Store the token with SDK v3 Secrets (Stream Deck 6.9+).

defects.title: Stream Deck plugin README omits /v1/recording
defects.claim: The plugin README (streamdeck/README.md:23) lists the endpoints a key press uses (`POST /v1/clip`, `/v1/screenshot` or `/v1/buffer`) but omits `/v1/recording`.
defects.scenario: Documentation of the control API used by the plugin is incomplete.
defects.fix: Add `/v1/recording` to the README (implied).

defects.title: Stream Deck inner package.json version disagrees with manifest
defects.claim: The inner `package.json` (streamdeck/com.einfabo.clippiboy.sdPlugin/package.json) says version 0.4.0 while the manifest says 0.6.5.0.
defects.scenario: Version metadata of the shipped plugin is inconsistent.
defects.fix: Align the versions (implied).

defects.title: streamdeck/install.ps1 uses npm install instead of npm ci
defects.claim: The dev-only `streamdeck/install.ps1` uses `npm install` rather than `npm ci` (noted under "Checked and fine"; otherwise it needs no admin and writes to `%APPDATA%` only).
defects.scenario: Dev installs may not reproduce the committed lockfile exactly.
defects.fix: Use `npm ci` (implied).

defects.title: Website has no security headers
defects.claim: The site proxy Worker (server/site-proxy/index.ts:29-43) passes GitHub Pages' headers through and only rewrites `Location`. clippiboy.com is served with no Content-Security-Policy, `X-Content-Type-Options`, `Referrer-Policy` or `frame-ancestors`. Risk is low because site/main.js is XSS-clean and there are no external scripts or fonts.
defects.scenario: No defense-in-depth against framing/clickjacking, MIME sniffing or a future XSS on clippiboy.com.
defects.fix: In the proxy, set `Content-Security-Policy: default-src 'self'; connect-src 'self' https://api.github.com; img-src 'self' data:; object-src 'none'; base-uri 'none'; frame-ancestors 'none'; form-action 'none'`, `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff` and `Referrer-Policy: strict-origin-when-cross-origin`, and enable HSTS at Cloudflare.

defects.title: Personal identifier in a public workers.dev hostname, which is also a second public origin
defects.claim: server/README.md:7,23 and server/scripts/e2e.mjs:11 contain the hostname `clippiboy-friends.fabian081964.workers.dev` (a first name plus number). server/wrangler.jsonc:12 keeps `"workers_dev": true`, so the friends Worker is publicly reachable on this second origin besides `api.clippiboy.com`.
defects.scenario: The maintainer's personal identifier is published in the public repo, and requests to the workers.dev origin bypass any zone-level WAF or rate-limit rules applied to `api.clippiboy.com`.
defects.fix: Plan to set `workers_dev: false` once old builds are gone, and scrub the name from docs.

defects.title: An unverified ffmpeg from the search path runs until the pinned copy is in place
defects.claim: src-tauri/src/muxer.rs:39-49 falls back to `_ => PathBuf::from(name)` when `TOOL_DIR` is unset or the pinned file is missing. Rust's `Command` on Windows then searches the exe's own directory (`%LOCALAPPDATA%\ClippiBoy`), then System32, then PATH, so any ffmpeg found that way runs without a hash check while the pinned download is pending ("The buffer already runs while that happens", site/index.html:191-192). This is the one gap in the otherwise end-to-end ffmpeg hash pinning.
defects.scenario: On first start, an `ffmpeg.exe` on PATH or next to the app is executed unverified. Same-user trust only, but it breaks the "tested build only" promise.
defects.fix: Refuse to fall back, or hash-check the fallback.

defects.title: tools/report invokes powershell by bare name (binary planting)
defects.claim: tools/report/src/main.rs:98-101 calls `Command::new("powershell")` by bare name. Rust resolves the application directory first, so a `powershell.exe` planted next to `clippiboy-report.exe` runs instead.
defects.scenario: The report exe is meant to be "sent around" (README:40-41) and usually lands in Downloads; a `powershell.exe` already present in Downloads is executed when the user runs `clippiboy-report.exe`.
defects.fix: Use `%SystemRoot%\System32\WindowsPowerShell\v1.0\powershell.exe`.

defects.title: rust-cache is probably useless for release builds
defects.claim: release.yml uses swatinem/rust-cache and the comment at .github/workflows/release.yml:35 expects reuse, but caches saved by a run on `refs/tags/vX` are visible only to that ref and to the default branch. No workflow builds Rust on main, so every release likely starts cold.
defects.scenario: Every tagged release compiles all ~740 crates from scratch despite the cache step.
defects.fix: A main-branch CI job (SC-P-1) would warm the cache.

defects.title: Non-draft release creation rests on a misconception and leaves an incomplete-latest window
defects.claim: .github/workflows/release.yml:66-67 says "Publishing as a draft would be safer, but the updater only sees finished releases." and therefore publishes immediately. The release could instead be created as a draft and published as the last step; publishing first creates a window where "latest" has no `latest.json` or no plugin attached.
defects.scenario: Between tauri-action publishing the release and the later `gh release upload`, the latest release lacks `latest.json` or the `.streamDeckPlugin`.
defects.fix: Create the release as a draft, upload the installer, `.sig`, `latest.json` and plugin, then run `gh release edit "$env:TAG" --draft=false` as the last step.

defects.title: LICENSE forbids copying/modifying while README tells readers to clone and build
defects.claim: LICENSE:16-18 forbids copying or modifying the source, while README.md:700-712 tells readers to clone and build it.
defects.scenario: Readers following the README's build instructions technically violate the LICENSE terms.
defects.fix: Clarify that a personal build is allowed.

defects.title: render-sounds.cjs installs an unpinned native npm module
defects.claim: scripts/render-sounds.cjs:7 uses an unpinned `npm i --no-save node-web-audio-api`, a native module with install scripts.
defects.scenario: Running the script installs whatever version is latest at that moment and runs its install scripts.
defects.fix: None stated explicitly; implied pinning of the version.

defects.title: Root .gitignore lacks .env and site/release.json
defects.claim: The root `.gitignore` does not list `.env` or `site/release.json`.
defects.scenario: A local `.env` or a generated `site/release.json` can be committed accidentally.
defects.fix: Add `.env` and `site/release.json` to `.gitignore` (implied).

defects.title: src-tauri/Cargo.toml lacks publish = false
defects.claim: `src-tauri/Cargo.toml` lacks `publish = false`.
defects.scenario: The proprietary crate could be published to crates.io by an accidental `cargo publish`.
defects.fix: Add `publish = false` (implied).

defects.title: README requires end-of-life Node 20+
defects.claim: README.md:715 says "Node 20+", which is end-of-life.
defects.scenario: Contributors are pointed at an EOL Node runtime.
defects.fix: Update the stated Node requirement (implied).

defects.title: Privacy page's "no IP stored" telemetry statement vs. enabled Workers observability logs
defects.claim: site/privacy.html says "Our server does not store your IP address with it" for the telemetry ping. That is true for the D1 rows, but the friends Worker has `"observability": {"enabled": true}` (server/wrangler.jsonc:8), so Workers Logs keep request metadata for /ping; this is disclosed only in the Friends section (site/privacy.html:93).
defects.scenario: A reader of the telemetry section is told the IP is not stored, while Cloudflare Workers Logs retain request metadata for /ping requests.
defects.fix: None stated (flagged as "Watch").

defects.title: Telemetry on by default with a persistent ID may need ePrivacy consent
defects.claim: Telemetry is on by default (src-tauri/src/config.rs:66) with a persistent random ID, justified as legitimate interest. Whether this needs consent under ePrivacy Art. 5(3) is a legal question.
defects.scenario: If consent is required, the default-on daily ping with a persistent ID would not be compliant.
defects.fix: None stated; legal question to resolve.

proposals.title: Add a CI quality-gate workflow (.github/workflows/ci.yml)
proposals.value: Catches broken commits before tag time, runs the 271 Rust tests and the server tests/type-check, checks generated schemas, audits advisories/licenses/duplicates, and warms the rust-cache for releases.
proposals.sketch: On push to main and pull_request, `permissions: { contents: read }`, concurrency `ci-${{ github.ref }}` with cancel-in-progress. Job `rust` (windows-latest): `actions/checkout@11d5960a326750d5838078e36cf38b85af677262` (v4.4.0) with `persist-credentials: false`; `rustup show` (honours rust-toolchain.toml); `Swatinem/rust-cache@6323deb102c322ba6fcbdcafc7e3dddab59af2b6` (v2.9.2) with workspaces `src-tauri` and `tools/report`; `npm ci --ignore-scripts && npm run build` (tauri-build needs ../dist); in src-tauri `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --locked --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo test --locked --lib`; `cargo build --locked --release --manifest-path tools/report/Cargo.toml`; `git diff --exit-code -- src-tauri/gen`. Job `web` (ubuntu-latest): `actions/setup-node@49933ea5288caeca8642d1e84afbd3f7d6820020` (v4.4.0) node 22 with npm cache; `npm ci && npm run build`; in server `npm ci && npm run check && npm test`; in streamdeck `npm ci && npm ci --prefix com.einfabo.clippiboy.sdPlugin && npm run build`; `npm audit --omit=dev --audit-level=high`. Job `audit`: `EmbarkStudios/cargo-deny-action@<sha>` with `manifest-path: src-tauri/Cargo.toml`, `command: check advisories licenses bans`.

proposals.title: Add Dependabot configuration
proposals.value: Keeps pinned action SHAs and cargo/npm dependencies current, so advisories like SC-11/SC-16 are surfaced automatically.

proposals.title: Harden release.yml (protected environment, version guard, draft-then-publish, checksums, provenance)
proposals.value: Protects the signing key, prevents mislabelled or trial releases, removes the incomplete-latest window, and gives users checksums and build provenance.
proposals.sketch: Job `windows`: `environment: release` (secrets live there; required reviewers; tag rule v*), `permissions: { contents: write, id-token: write, attestations: write }`; checkout pinned by SHA with `persist-credentials: false`; a "Tag must match versions" pwsh step (if tag ref, `env: TAG`) that reads versions from src-tauri/tauri.conf.json, package.json and src-tauri/Cargo.toml and throws if `"v$t" -ne $env:TAG -or $p -ne $t -or $c -ne $t`; node/rust setup pinned by SHA, `npm ci --ignore-scripts` where possible; `tauri-apps/tauri-action@84b9d35b5fc46c1e45415bdb6144030364f7ebc5` (v0.6.2, or v1.0.0 1deb371b…) with `tagName: ${{ startsWith(github.ref, 'refs/tags/') && github.ref_name || '' }}`, `releaseDraft: true`, `includeUpdaterJson: true`, `args: -- --locked`; a step computing SHA256SUMS of the setup.exe and .streamDeckPlugin via `Get-FileHash` and `gh release upload "$env:TAG" ... SHA256SUMS --clobber`; `actions/attest-build-provenance@<sha>` for `src-tauri/target/release/bundle/nsis/*-setup.exe`; final `gh release edit "$env:TAG" --draft=false --latest`; for non-tag runs `actions/upload-artifact@<sha>` with name `trial-build`.

proposals.title: Harden ffmpeg.yml and ship license/source info with the ffmpeg ZIP
proposals.value: Removes the ref_name injection pattern and credential persistence, and meets GPL redistribution obligations with attested artifacts.
proposals.sketch: Use `env: TAG: ${{ github.ref_name }}` with `$env:TAG`, `persist-credentials: false` and SHA-pinned actions; add gyan's LICENSE/README and a `SOURCE.txt` pointing to the exact source into the ZIP, and attest it.

proposals.title: Fail ffmpeg.yml when extracted hashes are not pinned in tools.rs
proposals.value: Guarantees the published ffmpeg ZIP matches the SHA-256s the app pins, so a release cannot ship binaries the app would reject.
proposals.sketch: pwsh step: `$src = Get-Content src-tauri/src/tools.rs -Raw; foreach ($e in 'ffmpeg.exe','ffprobe.exe') { $h=(Get-FileHash "dist-ffmpeg/$e" -A SHA256).Hash.ToLower(); if ($src -notmatch $h) { throw "$e $h not pinned in tools.rs" } }`.

proposals.title: Change repository settings for release integrity
proposals.value: Restricts who can trigger releases, prevents release-asset replacement, and gates access to the signing key.
proposals.sketch: Add a tag ruleset for `v*` and `ffmpeg-*`, turn on immutable releases, create the `release` environment with required reviewers, and add Authenticode signing through `bundle.windows.signCommand`.

proposals.title: Mask profile paths in the diagnostic report and add a review-before-sharing notice
proposals.value: The report contains COMPUTERNAME, USERNAME, full config.json, full logs, GPU/OS details, Run/Startup entries, the ffmpeg directory tree and 30 days of event-log hits; masking and a notice reduce accidental personal-data disclosure when it is sent around.
proposals.sketch: In tools/report/src/main.rs, mask user profile paths in collected output and print a "review before sharing" notice (alongside the existing `redact_token` at :213-243).

positives: ffmpeg hash pinning holds end to end: fetch-ffmpeg.mjs checks gyan.dev's essentials ZIP (from the GyanD/codexffmpeg mirror) against a pinned SHA-256 taken from gyan.dev's .sha256, and on first start the app checks both ffmpeg.exe and ffprobe.exe SHA-256s pinned in src-tauri/src/tools.rs:34-43 before moving them into place, so an upstream or asset swap is rejected (the one gap is SC-37).
The updater checks the minisign signature of latest.json/setup.exe against the pubkey in tauri.conf.json (key id 3E0633A2DA7AD3CE).
Lockfiles are committed with integrity hashes, all sourced from registry.npmjs.org and crates.io, and CI uses `npm ci`.
`workflow_run` in pages.yml is safe because `Release` cannot be triggered by PRs or forks.
No secrets are committed (pattern grep was clean; `*.key` and `*.pem` are gitignored).

The control port binds to 127.0.0.1, requires a token with a constant-time compare, and rejects requests carrying browser headers (`Origin`/`Referer`/`Sec-Fetch-Site`, src-tauri/src/control.rs:141-156).
ffmpeg.yml uses `--latest=false` correctly for the ffmpeg release.
There is a single `reqwest` (0.13.4) in the dependency tree and no aws-lc.
The zip RUSTSEC-2026-0367/-0368/-0369 advisories do not affect the app: src-tauri/src/tools.rs:265-283 uses `by_name` with its own hashing rather than `extract()`.
The Stream Deck plugin's runtime lockfile is clean under npm audit; all npm advisories are dev/build-time only.
Stream Deck property inspector (streamdeck/com.einfabo.clippiboy.sdPlugin/ui/settings.html) has no XSS: it uses `textContent` and `createElement` throughout.
streamdeck/install.ps1 is dev-only, needs no admin, and writes to `%APPDATA%` only.

site/main.js is XSS-clean: it uses `textContent` and `replaceChildren`, and validates `?ref=` against `/^[a-z0-9-]{1,32}$/` (site/main.js:385-386); there are no external scripts or fonts (Inter is self-hosted) and no `target=_blank`.

tools/report is read-only, writes only `clippiboy-report.txt` to the desktop and uploads nothing; `redact_token` (tools/report/src/main.rs:213-243) blanks `"token"` string values, which is enough today because the friends session lives in `friends.json`, which the tool does not read.

privacy.html is consistent with the code on: one ping a day with exactly the fields in server/src/telemetry.ts:21-56; the per-ref, per-day download counter (server/site-proxy/index.ts:67-75); iroh starting lazily only when a clip is sent (src-tauri/src/share.rs:878-893); 400-day retention (server/src/telemetry.ts:114-121); and no IP stored in the D1 rows.
